name: provisioner-bootstrap-plan decide(execute) → provisioner-bootstrap-execute
description: ADR-042 §addendum sandbox-bootstrap pack — provision path. Fires when plan terminates with decide(action=execute) — registry miss OR registry stale OR plan_hash changed. Spawns provisioner-bootstrap-execute, which runs docker commands per the plan (provision or re-provision) and prepares the tenant for verify.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.provisioner-bootstrap-execute
on_enter.prompt:
SANDBOX-BOOTSTRAP EXECUTE — run the plan against Docker.

The plan at loop $entity.instance emitted a provision or re-provision plan and stamped sandbox.tenant.* triples that the framework substitutes inline below. Your job is to materialise the plan: docker commands against the host daemon, executed via the always-warm sandbox's bash dispatch (the same bash tool research uses, with Docker socket access).

Your plan, resolved at spawn time:

- plan_action: $entity.triple.sandbox.tenant.plan_action
- signature: $entity.triple.sandbox.tenant.signature
- container_name: $entity.triple.sandbox.tenant.container_name
- base_image: $entity.triple.sandbox.tenant.image
- workspace: $entity.triple.sandbox.tenant.workspace
- clone_command: $entity.triple.sandbox.tenant.clone_command
- install_steps (JSON array; one shell line per entry): $entity.triple.sandbox.tenant.install_steps
- volume_mounts (JSON array; each entry is `<volume_name>:<container_path>`): $entity.triple.sandbox.tenant.volume_mounts
- docker_socket_mount (bool): $entity.triple.sandbox.tenant.docker_socket_mount
- verify_command (verify phase grades — do NOT run here): $entity.triple.sandbox.tenant.verify_command
- expected_smoke_signature (verify phase grades — audit only): $entity.triple.sandbox.tenant.expected_smoke_signature

Iteration 1 — if plan_action is `reprovision`, tear down the stale tenant first:
`bash docker rm -f <container_name>` (continues on `no such container` — already gone is fine).
Then for stale volumes (if the plan specifies fresh volumes): `bash docker volume rm <volume_name>` for each. Be conservative — only rm volumes the plan explicitly named for fresh start; reusing dep caches across provisions is a feature, not a bug.

Iteration 2 — create + start the tenant container:

```
bash docker run -d \
  --name <container_name> \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  <if docker_socket_mount: -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock> \
  <for each volume_mount: -v <mount>> \
  <base_image> \
  sleep infinity
```

The `sleep infinity` is the canonical idiom for "long-lived container that exists to be docker-exec'd into." Verify exit code 0 and that the container is `running` via `docker inspect`.

Iteration 3 — clone the source into the workspace (if clone_command is not `none`):
`bash docker exec <container_name> sh -c '<clone_command>'`
Capture exit code; non-zero is a hard failure — decide(needs_clarification) with the clone error.

Iteration 4+ — run install_steps sequentially. Parse the install_steps JSON array; for each step:
`bash docker exec <container_name> sh -c '<step>'`
Capture exit code per step. On non-zero, terminate decide(needs_clarification, reason="install step <N> failed: <step verbatim> — exit <code> — stderr <tail>"). The recovery rule routes to coordinator; the plan persona on retry can revise install_steps (drop the broken one, swap a dep version, etc.).

Long-running steps note: package installs and language-toolchain installs can take 5-30 minutes. The bash tool has its own per-call timeout (see semteams-shared memory feedback_sandbox_bash_timeouts). For steps you expect to be long-running (e.g. `apt-get install -y build-essential`, `go mod download`, `npm ci`), split into smaller idempotent steps where possible, OR document in scratchpad that this step is expected to be slow so the framework's iteration-budget signal doesn't mislead.

Iteration N − 1 — call emit_bootstrap_execute with the plan values you received in this prompt. The tool stamps sandbox.tenant.* triples on your loop entity so rule 03's spawn-prompt substitution resolves when verify is spawned:

```
emit_bootstrap_execute(
  signature="<echo $entity.triple.sandbox.tenant.signature>",
  container_name="<echo $entity.triple.sandbox.tenant.container_name>",
  image="<echo $entity.triple.sandbox.tenant.image>",
  workspace="<echo $entity.triple.sandbox.tenant.workspace>",
  plan_hash="<echo $entity.triple.sandbox.tenant.plan_hash>",
  plan_action="<echo $entity.triple.sandbox.tenant.plan_action>",
  verify_command="<echo $entity.triple.sandbox.tenant.verify_command>",
  expected_smoke_signature="<echo $entity.triple.sandbox.tenant.expected_smoke_signature>"
)
```

This is pure plumbing — every arg is a verbatim echo of the value already in your prompt. The tool has no canonicalization or registry mutation; it just forwards triples onto your loop entity.

Iteration N — terminate: decide(action="verify", reason="tenant <container_name> provisioned: base=<image> clone=<source@ref> installed=<N steps>; ready for smoke check"). Rule 03 spawns verify; verify's prompt substitutes the values you stamped above.

Iteration budget — execute is the most LLM-iteration-intensive role in this pack (one iteration per install step). If the plan has 20+ install steps, batch them where idempotent (a single `apt-get install -y A B C D E` is one step, not 5). If the plan was authored with too many fine-grained steps, scratchpad note + batch.

Per ADR-041 addendum 2026-05-15: chain agents do not query the graph. read_loop_result + bash are your read channels.

metadata.docker_socket_access: Execute uses the always-warm sandbox's bash, which has Docker socket access (PR #179 + the §A foundation PR's mount config). The tenant containers are spawned on the same host daemon. The tenant gets ITS OWN docker socket mount only if the plan.docker_socket_mount=true (for testcontainers / docker-compose targets).
metadata.long_step_timeout_caveat: Individual install steps can hit per-bash-call timeout (semteams-shared feedback_sandbox_bash_timeouts memory). Mitigation: batch idempotent steps, document slow ones in scratchpad. Future substrate question: per-call timeout overrides on the bash tool for tenant-execute roles.
metadata.tool_choice_rationale: Required-mode forces gemini-flash through every bash + decide. Without it, mid-iteration text-only completions during install_steps would strand work (research-pack semstreams#158 class).
